# Talos

> An autonomous AI agent you can hand a shell to. It can prove what it will not do. Tool calls pass a small permission kernel (allow / needs-human / deny). Runs land in a hash-chained audit log. Updates are Ed25519-signed tarballs, verified before anything is unpacked.

## Facts

- Permission kernel: 996 lines of Python, the only code that decides
- 37 tools, all gated; unattended runs cannot escalate
- 3492 tests collected in the source tree; 277/277 red-team cases passed in source verification. Release contents follow their own signed tag.
- MCP servers run only inside a UID-separated worker, from an operator-owned registry — no marketplace, no third-party code in the agent process
- Channels: Telegram, mail (IMAP pull), CLI, WhatsApp via an operator-controlled broker — every channel fetches; no inbound port, no webhook
- Updates: signed tarballs, verified before anything is unpacked; dependencies pinned and hashed, installed with --require-hashes
- Latest signed release: 0.20.0. Includes safe migration, Talos Connections and labelled scheduled-result notifications.
- Migration in 0.20.0: fingerprinted redacted preview, inactive staging apply, recovery archive and one-at-a-time validated skill activation; no inherited secrets or authority
- Talos Connections in 0.20.0: isolated-worker inventory plus disabled secret-free drafts; no bundled account, endpoint or private service
- Scheduled runs on current source stay quiet while working and deliver one labelled final result; interactive work trails show bounded skill and executable names without arguments or contents
- License: MIT
